additional_concerns: Paragraph 3.11 and the answer to question 1 of the SFC's Code of Conduct FAQs issued on 30 September 2010 are referenced but not supplied as external dependencies. The circular supports the stated gift rule, but does not establish the complete external classification standards.

node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e puts offering in scope; node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5, node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5, node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 put promotional linkage in scope. Consequently, failure of these conditions returns OUT_OF_SCOPE rather than a Boolean answer. Whether this matches the intended question domain remains unresolved.

The offer-level candidates establish promotional linkage for the offer and gift classification for a component separately. They need an attribution rule ensuring the identified gift component has the required promotional connection; mere inclusion in a mixed offer may not establish that connection.
The SFC-authorised-fund limitations have support in the circular's opening scope. They should not be interpreted as establishing the full scope of paragraph 3.11 outside this circular.
Gift-control compliance or a component not being caught does not establish compliance with paragraph 2.3, section 103, or the circular's other requirements.
